_comment: Example only. Every name here is invented.
A real terms file lists the exact strings you are trying not to publish,
so it belongs OUTSIDE the repository being audited. gitsieve refuses a
--terms path inside the repo unless you pass --allow-terms-in-repo.
What can safely live in the repo is a file like this one: suppressions
and controls that reference terms by id, never by value.

terms.note: non-ASCII spelling; no word boundaries applied
not scanned in identities; nobody's name contains it
also an ordinary word; see the suppression below

controls.value: a string you know for a fact is in this repository's file contents
controls.note: checked with the same matcher a real term uses; zero matches means the run is untrusted

suppress.reason: delta as in difference; unrelated to the organisation name
AWS's own published example key id, planted in a test fixture; not a credential
